items.title: SW: Space War Program for Stanford A.I. Project (SAIL file SW[SW,REG]), sixteen versions, November 1972 to September 1977
items.creator: Gorin, Ralph E.
items.source: Wayback Machine copies (14 January 2024) of saildart.org SW[SW,REG]1 to SW[SW,REG]16
items.description: The SAIL Space War source as kept in the [SW,REG] disk area, in sixteen dated versions from 4 November 1972 to 22 September 1977 (version 11, dated 11 November 1975, is a binary shown as octal). Each text version opens "TITLE SW SPACE WAR PROGRAM FOR STANFORD A.I. PROJECT" with the revision comment "REVISED SEPTEMBER 5,1971 R.E. GORIN" and "FEB 1972 R TAYLOR"; versions 15 and 16 (August and September 1977) add a D. Woods revision line. The page directory includes "THE PDP-6 SPACE WAR MODULE", "THE MINE CALCULATIONS" and "INSERT LOSER INTO NEW HYPERSPACE". The series runs between the held SW[SW,BGB] (18 September 1973) and SW.OLD[CSP,SYS] (29 September 1977) and records the program's changes over five years in the area that also holds Maurer's Fortran SPCWAR.F4[SW,REG] (held). A SRCCOM file, SW.DIF[ACT,REG] (1 February 1976), compares SW[SW,REG] with DF[1,LIS], a "DOG FIGHT PROGRAM FOR STANFORD A.I. PROJECT" derived from it.

items.title: SPCWAR by D.E. Wrege, Version 3 (SPCWR3.PA, PAL8 source for the PDP-12, PDP-8/E VC8E, AX08 and Type 30G displays), copyright 1974
items.creator: Wrege, D. E.
items.source: Wayback Machine copy (29 December 2015) of pdp8.net's OS/8 file viewer, SPCWR3.PA from the DECtape image images/jby/jbyos8.tu56 (blocks 510-640); pdp8.net is now offline
items.rights: "COPYRIGHT (C) 1974 BY D.E. WREGE & ASSOC."; licensed to Georgia Tech "for use on a single computer system" (as in the file)
items.description: PDP-8 family assembly source headed "/SPCWAR BY D.E. WREGE / VERSION 3" and "SPACE WAR. V3", with a copyright notice for D.E. Wrege & Assoc. and a licence clause stating the software "IS FURNISHED TO GEORGIA TECH. UNDER A LICENSE FOR USE ON A SINGLE COMPUTER SYSTEM". Conditional assembly selects the display: AX08 (LAB-8), Type 30G, PDP-8/E VC8E, or by default the PDP-12 VR12 in LINC mode ("/PDP-12 - VR12 IS DEFAULT"). Variables and routines include gravity (QGRAV), the sun (SUN, DSUN) and hyperspace (HYPERS). The copy was read from an OS/8 DECtape image (jbyos8.tu56) on pdp8.net; in 2018 the Rhode Island Computer Museum reported modifying this source to read PDP-12 GPIO switch boxes (cctech, 23 September 2018). The same text is in the spacewar1962/spacewar repository, labelled LINC-8/PDP-12; the file itself is PAL8, not LAP6.
items.extent: PAL8 source, 2,498 lines (47,723 bytes)
items.machine: DEC PDP-12 (VR12), PDP-8/E (VC8E), LAB-8 (AX08) or Type 30G

items.title: DUEL: two-ship display game for the PDP-15 (MACRO-15 source DUEL SRC and DUELOK SRC), University of Waterloo DECtape 102
items.creator: Unknown
items.description: Assembly source headed ".TITLE DUEL" for a PDP-7/9/15 family machine with a vector display (display IOTs such as IDLA=700606), found on a University of Waterloo DECtape whose label reads "102 17-MAR-77" (the label date, not a date in the file). Two ships, each with a rotating turret, move forward and backward with drift, turn left and right, and fire (routines FOR1/FOR2, REV1/REV2, LEFT1/LEFT2, RT1/RT2, FIRE1/FIRE2, DRIFT; comment "ESTABLISH DIRECTION COMPONENTS OF TURRET OF SHIP 1"), with fire single, continuous and stop on switches and an A/D converter input. No sun or gravity code was found. The name matches DECUS 7-40 DUEL (Peterson and Viner, Cambridge, PDP-7 and 340, catalogued as "very similar to SPACE-WAR"), but nothing in the file names its authors, so the identification is unconfirmed. The rest of the tape holds music files (carols, TUNE, HARMON) and a MOON program.
items.extent: DUEL 1,151 lines (11,931 bytes); DUELOK 1,003 lines (10,291 bytes); zip with directory, tape labels and manifest

items.title: Galaxy Game: PDP-11 source code (GalaxyGame_compile11.mac, OCR transcription version 1.2.2)
items.creator: Pitts, Bill
items.description: Assembly source for Galaxy Game, the coin-operated PDP-11 version of Spacewar! that Bill Pitts and Hugh Tuck installed at Stanford's Tresidder Union in 1971. The header comments say it is "one of the first Arcade games", "Created by Bill Pitts and Hugh Tuck in 1971", written for the PDP-11 in machine language, and "OCR and Typed By Quantum Leaper" with help from "Rob and Gatinho" (version 1.2.2); the code defines the coin accumulator (COINAC), display X and Y registers and two terminals (NTERM = 2). The date of the original printout behind the transcription is not stated. It does not name MIT or Russell.
items.extent: 27 KB, 2,270 lines of MACRO-11

items.title: cromemco_spacewar.ptp: Cromemco Dazzler SPACEWAR paper-tape image
items.creator: Cromemco, Inc.
items.description: Binary image of a Cromemco paper tape of SPACEWAR for the Dazzler, one of a set of Cromemco game tapes (Chase, Tankwar, Track, Magenta Martini, 4D Tic Tac Toe and others) read for bitsavers in 2004. Cromemco advertised SPACEWAR on $15 paper tape in Creative Computing in early 1977 (P-XA8X4) and the NMAH holds a 1976 Cromemco SPACEWAR tape with documentation (P-0G3ZP). The image begins with leader and Z-80/8080 code (a jump instruction at offset 0x41); no text identifies an author. Date of the tape not stated (1976-77 by the related records).
items.extent: 3,906 bytes (binary paper-tape image)

items.title: orbit: "Spacewar on the Sun", by Bob Bane (C and 68000 assembly source for the Sun workstation, files dated 22 August 1983)
items.creator: Bane, Bob
items.publisher: University of Maryland, Computer Science (inferred from the README address bane.umcp-cs)
items.source: GitHub PDP-10/Spacewar, branch not-pdp10, orbit.tar.gz (commit 3781a0e22b7a, 15 October 2019, "Spacewar for Unix.")
items.description: A Spacewar for the Sun workstation under Berkeley 4.2-derived Unix, recovered in 2019 from a Lisp Machine tape labelled in masking tape "SPACEWAR FOR VAX (Unix?)" (Daniel Seagraves, cctalk, 15 October 2019). The manual page reads "orbit - Spacewar on the Sun ... The classic game of interplanetary death and destruction. Mostly written in C; an assembler package does fast single-precision floating-point for orbital calculations and collision detection", with adjustable parameters (Gravity, Thrust, TurnSpeed, RateBomb, LifeTimeBomb) saved in option files and a ship designer (prepship). The README, signed "Bob Bane (bane.umcp-cs@UDel-Relay)", says it "should work with no changes on Berkeley 4.2"; updown.c includes the Sun ROM-vector header. All files are dated 22 August 1983 in the tar listing.
items.extent: gzip tar, 30,405 bytes (136,192 bytes unpacked); 53 files including orbit.man, README, C sources, fp.s, sorbit.s and ship designs

items.title: Spacewar! PDP-1 emulator Java applet, with retyped Spacewar 3.1 source and Perl PDP-1 assembler (Silverman, Silverman and Gerasimov, MIT Media Lab), sources dated 18 December 1996
items.creator: Silverman, Barry
items.publisher: MIT Media Laboratory, Epistemology and Learning group
items.source: Wayback Machine captures of http://lcs.www.media.mit.edu/groups/el/projects/spacewar/ (page 6 December 1998, readme 24 February 1999, sources directory 15 July 2001)
items.rights: "Spacewar! is in the public domain, but this credit paragraph must accompany all distributed versions of the program." (readme); no separate statement for the Java and Perl code
items.description: A web re-creation that runs the PDP-1 Spacewar! binary on a PDP-1 emulator written as a Java applet. The readme, signed Barry Silverman, Brian Silverman and Vadim Gerasimov, says: "Martin Graetz provided us with a printed version of the source. We typed in in again - it was about 40 pages long - and re-assembled it with a PDP-1 assembler written in PERL", with two changes (bigger ships and special-cased timing), and gives the keys for the two players. The sources directory lists all files dated 18 December 1996; the retyped source is headed "/spacewar 3.1 24 sep 62". The applet page (pdp1b.class) is captured from 6 December 1998. Compiled class files and spacewar.bin were not copied.
items.extent: zip 77,733 bytes: applet page, readme, directory listing and 10 source files (Java applet and front panel, Perl assembler passes, spacewar.mac 31,991 bytes, spacewar.lst 233,062 bytes)
items.progLanguage: Java (PDP-1 emulator), with PDP-1 MACRO source
items.machine: Java applet in a web browser

parents.evidence: Readme: Graetz provided a printed source, which was typed in again and re-assembled (P-3XRMR).

items.title: SPACEWAR for the IBM PC and PCjr, by Bill Seiler, versions 1.50 (1985) and 1.70 (1986)
items.creator: Seiler, Bill
items.source: Internet Archive, SPACEWAR_1020 (collection classicpcgames), files SpacewarV1.50sw1985billSeileraction.zip, SpacewarV1.50a1sw1985billSeileraction.zip, SpacewarV1.50o1sw1985billSeileraction.zip, SpacewarV1.70sw1986billSeileraction.zip
items.rights: "SPACEWAR COPYRIGHT 1985,1986 B SEILER." Distributed as user-supported software: "You are encouraged to copy and share this program with other users. Please do not remove the copyright or the user-supported notice." (SPACEWAR.DOC, version 1.70)
items.description: A two-player Spacewar for the IBM PC Color Graphics Card (640 x 200) and PCjr by Bill Seiler, co-author of the 1974 PDP-11 Space War (DECUS 11-192, held). SPACEWAR.DOC (version 1.70, read inside the IA zip) gives photon torpedoes, phasers, impulse engines, cloak and hyperspace, shield and weapon energy recharged from "Dilithium crystals", left and right "Auto Robot" players, and function keys that place "a Gravity hole" or "a Planet at the center of the screen". It offered the source code on floppy for a $30 contribution. Also on IA as msdos_Spacewar_1985 (MobyGames-derived record, "a shareware Spacewar! variant") and Spacewar_dos (an Italian-language version, SWC.EXE, described there as based on Seiler's 1985 original). Held as a link; binaries not downloaded.
items.extent: DOS program; version 1.70 zip holds SPACEWAR.EXE (22,528 bytes, 6 May 1986) and SPACEWAR.DOC (6,832 bytes, 16 August 1986)

parents.evidence: Seiler co-wrote the 1974 PDP-11 Space War (P-6H9SS); the PC program does not state a link.

JAEGER / APX-20224". The IA description, credited there to MobyGames, says two ships fly around a sun with Newtonian thrust, the sun's gravity can be positive, negative or off in five strengths, the field can wrap or bounce, and the point limit can be 10, 21 or none. items.title: Space Wars (Vectrex cartridge, GCE, 1982)
items.rights: None stated on the IA page
items.description: The Vectrex home version of Space Wars, the vector-display two-player game with a central star that Cinematronics released in the arcade in 1977 (arcade material on that game is already held as paratexts). The box art on the IA page reads "Vectrex Arcade System Cartridge / SPACE WARS", shows two ships, their trails and a central star, labels "PLAYER ONE" and "PLAYER TWO", and is credited to GCE. items.title: Space War / Space Combat (Atari 2600 cartridge CX2604), the game program
items.creator: Shepard, Ian (programmer, per the IA identifier)
items.rights: None stated on the IA page
items.description: The playable Atari VCS / 2600 Space War of 1978, also sold by Sears as Space Combat. The IA description calls it "an Atari 2600 port of Spacewar!, the famous 1962 computer game by Steve Russell" with 17 variations, 1 to 13 being two-ship duels, some "near a planet which has gravitational attraction". The programmer's name (Ian Shepard) and Sears number appear only in the IA identifier. The archive already holds the instruction booklet and box and cartridge scans; this record adds the game program itself as a link. A home-console cartridge image, not an arcade ROM; not downloaded.

items.title: SpaceWar 1.0.4 for the Macintosh, by Dan Frohlich (freeware, 1994)

items.description: A Macintosh SpaceWar for one or two players, year given as 1994 on the Macintosh Repository page. The quoted description reads: "In SpaceWar each player, attempts to destroy the other by blasting him with energy torpedos. While avoiding the various hazzards common in a space arcade game", with rendered graphics, one- and two-player modes, configurable controls and "Many Game Options". The page does not mention the PDP-1 original, so the lineage rests on the name and the two-player torpedo duel. Not found in the Info-Mac archive mirror at the University of Michigan (game/war and game/space directories). Held as a link; not downloaded.
